reading.text:
Reading of spec ex_dealer_potential (Example 5.5, "The potential V is even and convex, with
grad V(w) = w/sqrt(1+|w|^2), |grad V(w)| <= 1, Lip(grad V) <= 1").

Setting: the fibre L^2(nu;R^m) of the standing setting; in Example 5.5 (built on Example 5.1(i))
n=m=d=1, so the fibre is L^2(nu;R), for every sigma-finite nu on a countably generated (E,cE)
(nu = 0 and nu(E)=infinity included). A statement over an arbitrary real inner-product /
Hilbert space is broader and fine (instantiation: the space L^2(nu;R) or L^2(nu;R^m)).

Objects: V(w) := sqrt(1 + |w|^2) - 1 with |.| the L^2(nu) norm; gradV(w) := w / sqrt(1+|w|^2).

A faithful statement must contain, for every w, w' in the fibre:
 1. evenness: V(-w) = V(w);
 2. convexity of V on the whole space (ConvexOn R univ V);
 3. "its gradient": gradV(w) is the gradient of V at w, i.e. V is (Frechet) differentiable at
    every w with derivative the functional <gradV(w), .> (HasGradientAt / HasFDerivAt with
    innerSL). A statement that only defines gradV by the formula and never links it to the
    derivative of V would lose this clause (narrower);
 4. boundedness: |gradV(w)| <= 1 for every w;
 5. 1-Lipschitz: |gradV(w) - gradV(w')| <= |w - w'| for all w, w' (LipschitzWith 1).
No hypotheses beyond the setting. Constants are absolute (1). Junk values: sqrt is applied to
1+|w|^2 >= 1 so no junk; division by sqrt(...) >= 1 is never by zero.
The witness question does not arise (no hypotheses), except that the space is arbitrary.

comparison.text:
Comparison, ex_dealer_potential (Sec5.lean:648-656).
Setting: Lean quantifies over every measure nu on every measurable space E (reading: sigma-finite
on countably generated E). Broader ambient setting; the fibre is Lp (EuclideanSpace R (Fin 1)) 2
nu = L^2(nu;R), as in Example 5.5 (n=m=d=1). Instantiation: restrict to sigma-finite nu.
V w := sqrt(1+|w|^2) - 1 and gradV w := (sqrt(1+|w|^2))^{-1} . w: the printed formulas (inverse
of a number >= 1, no junk).
Items:
 1. evenness: (forall w, V (-w) = V w) - present.
 2. convexity: ConvexOn R univ V - present.
 3. gradient: forall w, HasGradientAt V (gradV w) w - present, the derivative identity (not
    only the formula). Lp 2 is complete, so HasGradientAt is the Frechet derivative <gradV w, .>.
 4. |gradV w| <= 1 for all w - present.
 5. |gradV w - gradV w'| <= |w - w'| for all w, w' - present (1-Lipschitz).
No hypotheses; nothing narrower. Verdict: faithful.
